name: Cissus

project_scope.source_pool: Master Plant Pool row 269, 15 wild-tagged iNaturalist observations, PASS verified Travis Bexar Comal
project_scope.note: Single-species Cissus lesson; compares installed Vitis species. Parthenocissus under an independent active work claim; do not overwrite that lesson.

look_here_first: FIRST locate the node: Cissus trifoliata has relatively fleshy foliage usually divided into THREE leaflets (sometimes deeply three-parted), whereas Vitis typically has ONE simple leaf, even if deeply lobed. Then check unbranched tendril, red/brown warty stem nodes, small greenish flower clusters, and dark berries. Do not identify Cissus from three lobes alone.
shared_genus_recognition: Woody-based scrambling or climbing vine in the grape family, Vitaceae
Leaves alternate, with the common regional Cissus trifoliata possessing three-parted or trifoliolate foliage; trace leaflet stalks to the main petiole to separate leaflets from lobes
Tendrils usually slender and unbranched, commonly opposite foliage on shoots; nodes can be swollen/warty or reddish
Flowers small greenish in clusters, much less conspicuous than passionflowers; fruit dark berries
decision_sequence: 1. Find a whole leaf attachment and count separately jointed leaflets; a lobe is part of one continuous blade, not a separate leaflet.
2. Follow the petiole to a Cissus leaflet joint, then find the opposite tendril and inspect branching.
3. Check flexible to woody reddish node and glossy/thicker leaflet texture; compare with Vitis simple leaf or Parthenocissus thinner radiating leaflets.
4. Inspect flowers and fruit only in conjunction with leaf architecture; round berries alone do not prove a genus.
5. If variation or photo cropping hides nodes and leaflet joints, keep ID at Vitaceae until a full shoot is visible.

lookalike_cautions: Do not mistake a deeply three-lobed Vitis blade for a three-leaflet Cissus leaf. Inspect the leaflet junction at petiole.
Virginia creeper / thicket creeper can be 3-foliolate at juvenile nodes; leaflet count must be combined with tendril type and stem architecture.
Leaf arrangement and tendril attachment matter more than fruit color alone.
Cissus trifoliata has a verified native-range PASS; do not automatically confer the same county status on unreviewed Cissus species.

taxonomy_note: Cissus incisa Des Moulins is a synonym of the accepted Cissus trifoliata under Flora of North America; make no duplicate canonical C. incisa card. C. trifoliata leaves are USUALLY three-foliolate, SOMETIMES simple but three-lobed, rarely unlobed. Leaf architecture alone is best read with tendril and node.
fna_congener_note: FNA recognizes Cissus verticillata as another species in the flora, generally with simple unlobed hairy blades, unlike glabrous trifoliolate / simple 3-lobed C. trifoliata. Not a target for canonical installation without source pool and range review.
